snippets.title: Moving money between accounts
snippets.prompt: An in-memory bank used by a multi-threaded payments simulator. Accounts are opened while transfers run on other threads, and transfer may be called concurrently in any direction. total() is used by a health check that runs while transfers are in flight.
code: private final Map<String, Account> accounts = new HashMap<>();
public void open(String id, double openingBalance) {
public void transfer(String fromId, String toId, double amount) {

issues.summary: Locks are taken in argument order. transfer(a, b) on one thread and transfer(b, a) on another each take their first lock and wait forever for the second: a deadlock.
issues.fix: Always lock the two accounts in one global order, for example by id (lock the smaller id first), or use a single lock for transfers.

issues.summary: Balances are doubles, so amounts like 0.10 are not exact and repeated transfers drift by fractions of a cent.
issues.fix: Hold money as a long count of cents, or BigDecimal.

issues.summary: A negative amount is not rejected: it passes the balance check and moves money from the destination into the source, so anyone who can call transfer can drain any account.

A plain HashMap is read and written from several threads (open runs while transfers do), which can corrupt it or hide new accounts; total() also reads balances with no lock, so it can see a transfer half done.
issues.fix: Use a ConcurrentHashMap, and read the balances under the same locking the transfers use.

issues.summary: An unknown id gives a null account, and synchronized (null) throws a NullPointerException that says nothing about the bad id.
issues.fix: Check both lookups and throw an IllegalArgumentException naming the unknown account.

snippets.explanation: Two locks taken in caller-chosen order is the textbook deadlock. With money, also check the type that holds it and every value a caller controls, including the sign.

snippets.title: Reading admins from a CSV file
snippets.prompt: Imports users from a CSV export with lines like 'ada@example.com,Ada Lovelace,admin' and returns the admins; contains() checks whether a user is in a list. The export ends with a blank line.
code: public List<User> readAdmins(String path) throws IOException {
public boolean contains(List<User> users, User candidate) {

issues.summary: role == "admin" compares references, not text. The role comes from split and trim, a different String object, so the test is never true and no admin is ever returned.
i <= users.size() runs one past the end, so whenever the candidate is not in the list, users.get(size) throws IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning false.
issues.fix: Use i < users.size(), or simply return users.contains(candidate) (records compare by value).

issues.summary: The reader is never closed, so every call leaks a file handle, and an exception mid-file leaks it too.
issues.fix: Open it in try-with-resources: try (BufferedReader reader = new BufferedReader(new FileReader(path))) { ... }.

issues.summary: The blank last line splits into one empty field, so parts[2] throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and the whole import fails.
issues.fix: Skip blank lines and check parts.length >= 3 (reporting a malformed line) before reading the fields.

snippets.explanation: Java's == on objects, an off-by-one bound and an unclosed resource are the three bugs a reviewer should spot on sight. Then feed the parser the input the prompt promised: a blank line.
